summary: Iteration 14 — CSV product-import feature. Ran 16 pytest cases covering auth gates, Shopify grouping, image fetch/storage, draft hiding on public list & detail, draft checkout blocking, publish gates, publish-all skipped_details, size/count caps, and backward compat. All 16 backend tests PASS. Frontend E2E via Playwright: login → /brand/import loads with all data-testids → upload sample Shopify CSV → toast 'Imported 1 products as drafts' → summary card shows '1 imported as drafts · 1 skipped' with skipped-row table (row 4, Broken, missing or invalid price) → 1 draft card rendered → clicking publish-draft removed it from grid (1→0) → dashboard shows import-csv-button. Grouping correct: 2 variants of ui-test-hoodie collapsed into single product; no-price row skipped with row# + reason. Verified images are stored under /api/files/... (external unsplash URLs NOT leaked into product.images).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/imports.py uses blocking `http_requests.get` (requests library) inside an async endpoint — for large imports this blocks the event loop for up to (20s * N images). Consider aiohttp/httpx.AsyncClient or running the fetch loop via asyncio.to_thread to keep the API responsive under concurrency. Not a functional bug, but a scaling smell.

_build_product_doc silently pads short descriptions with a placeholder rather than skipping — acceptable UX-wise, but means publish blocker 'description too short' can never trigger on freshly-imported drafts. Fine given publish gate re-validates.

MAX_IMPORT_PRODUCTS check happens AFTER _extract_rows + _group_rows already ran — for a malicious 5MB CSV of 200k tiny rows this could be memory-heavy. Consider counting rows during parse and bailing early. Low priority given 5MB file cap already limits blast radius.
seed_data_creation: Created 2 draft products during test; cleanup teardown deletes them via DELETE /api/products/{id}. Frontend test published then deleted its own drafts.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CSV import feature fully working. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_csv_import.py is reusable regression. NOTE: /api/orders/checkout requires an `origin_url` field in the body (not documented in review request but needed to reproduce checkout tests). Draft checkout correctly 404s. Backend logs are clean; no ObjectId serialization issues observed.
